results.name: IIT Madras Chip Startup Discovered Materials Gets $9 Million In Seed Funding
results.content:
Advait Sridhar and Akash Ramdas, both alumni of IIT Madras, have founded Discovered Materials, a startup that recently secured $9 million (Rs 85 crore) in seed funding led by Lightspeed India Partners. The company is targeting a critical challenge in artificial intelligence development: AI chips generate heat exceeding 140 watts per square centimetre. Discovered Materials will use AI agents to discover new materials for semiconductor chips, initially focusing on thermal management solutions across the entire semiconductor stack.
## Discovered Materials Secures $9 Million Seed Funding Led by Lightspeed  
AI chip thermal challenges are driving demand for novel materials, as evidenced by a recent $9 million seed funding round secured by Discovered Materials. The seed funding round was led by Lightspeed India Partners, with substantial participation from [Y Combinator](https://entangledfuture.com/company/y-combinator/), Peak XV Partners, and several prominent angel investors including Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram, and Thariq Shihipar.  
This investor base signals strong early confidence in the company’s approach to materials discovery. Discovered Materials is developing AI agents designed to accelerate the identification of materials with optimal properties for semiconductor applications, initially concentrating on those that improve heat dissipation.  
The company’s technology extends beyond thermal management, with ambitions to discover materials across the entire semiconductor stack. The founders’ connection to IIT Madras appears to be a key element of the company’s origins and early success; both Sridhar and Ramdas are alumni of the institution, suggesting a strong foundation in engineering and technology.
The company believes that a proactive approach to materials science is essential for continued progress in artificial intelligence, and the team aims to fundamentally alter the materials discovery process. Traditional materials discovery is slow, expensive, and often relies on chance; by employing AI agents, the company hopes to significantly reduce both the time and cost associated with identifying and validating new materials.  
The initial focus on thermal management reflects the immediate and pressing needs of the AI industry, but the long-term vision encompasses a broader range of semiconductor materials. The company plans to expand its AI-driven platform to address challenges in areas such as power efficiency, signal processing, and device miniaturization.  
The $9 million in funding will be used to expand the company’s research and development efforts, scale its AI platform, and build a team of materials scientists and engineers. Discovered Materials intends to establish partnerships with leading semiconductor manufacturers to accelerate the adoption of its new materials, ultimately aiming to become a leading provider of innovative materials solutions for the semiconductor industry and enable the development of more powerful, efficient, and sustainable AI technologies.

results.content:
# Discovered Materials Raises $9 Million in Seed Funding Led by Lightspeed India Partners  
The startup was previously known as Matforge and is part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch.  
[Rosalin Biswal](https://www.ceovine.com/author/rosalin-biswal)•August 14, 2026  
Deeptech startup Discovered Materials has raised $9 million (approximately ₹85 crore) in a seed funding round led by [Lightspeed India Partners](https://www.ceovine.com/tag/lightspeed), with participation from [Y Combinator](https://www.ceovine.com/tag/y-combinator), [Peak XV Partners](https://www.ceovine.com/tag/peak-xv) and angel investors including Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram and Thariq Shihipar.  
The San Francisco-based startup, founded by IIT Madras alumni **Akash Ramdas** and **Advaith Sridhar**, will use the fresh capital to expand its team, build laboratory infrastructure and advance its AI agents for materials discovery, with an initial focus on materials for semiconductor applications.  
Announcing the funding, Sridhar said in an X post that the company is focused on building AI scientists capable of accelerating materials research and moving discoveries from computation to physical validation.  
> Today, we're introducing
>
> — Advaith Sridhar (@advaith\_sridhar)[@discoveredmat](). We build AI scientists that discover new materials for semiconductor chips.
> We’re starting by releasing our work – hundreds of new materials discovered using frontier AI models, along with our benchmark for tracking progress in this…[pic.twitter.com/1UdMjgjFQY]()[August 10, 2026]()  
Discovered Materials is developing AI systems designed to work across the materials discovery process, including simulation, synthesis and experimental validation. The company aims to use AI agents to identify promising materials, determine how they can be synthesised and validate their performance through laboratory experiments.  
The startup is particularly focused on materials for thermal management in advanced semiconductors. As AI processors become increasingly powerful, managing the heat generated by high-performance chips has emerged as a major challenge for the semiconductor industry. Discovered Materials is working on materials that could improve heat dissipation and support technologies such as advanced semiconductor packaging and 3D chip stacking.  
According to the company, its AI systems can explore thousands of potential material candidates, compared with the limited number researchers can typically evaluate manually. The startup says its systems have already identified hundreds of potential new materials and several candidates with properties comparable to materials currently used by major chipmakers, although the specific compositions have not been disclosed.
The company is also developing Material Discovery Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on real-world materials-discovery problems. The benchmark aims to measure whether AI systems can move beyond generating theoretical candidates and solve materials problems that can ultimately be validated experimentally.  
Discovered Materials plans to patent promising discoveries and eventually license the resulting technologies to semiconductor companies, giving the startup an intellectual-property-driven business model alongside its AI technology.  
Co-founder **Akash Ramdas** has a PhD and postdoctoral research background in materials science from Stanford University, while **Advaith Sridhar** holds a master’s degree in artificial intelligence from Carnegie Mellon University. The founders first met at IIT Madras and bring expertise across materials science, artificial intelligence and autonomous AI systems.  
The startup was previously known as**Matforge**and is part of Y Combinator’s Spring 2026 batch. Its latest funding comes as semiconductor companies and data-centre operators face growing challenges around chip performance, powerconsumptionand thermal management.

results.content:
# Discovered Materials Raises $9 Million Seed Round To Speed Up Chip Material Discovery With AI  
Discovered Materials has raised $9 million in seed funding at a time when the chip industry is looking for answers beyond just smaller transistors and faster processors. The startup is working on a hard but important problem – finding new materials that can make semiconductor chips more efficient, cooler and easier to scale.  
The seed round was led by Lightspeed India Partners. Y Combinator, Peak XV Partners and angel investors including Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram and Thariq Shihipar also participated. As per reports, the funding is about Rs. 85 crore.  
At the heart of the company’s plan is a simple idea. If AI is creating a huge demand for more computing power, then AI can also help find the materials needed to support that demand.
## The Main Purpose Of The Funding  
The aim of the funding is not just to grow quickly like a normal software startup. Discovered Materials needs capital to build a research engine that can move from idea to lab-tested material faster than traditional methods.  
There are three clear purposes behind this seed round.  
1. First, the company wants to scale its AI agents. These agents need to understand scientific problems, generate useful material ideas and help researchers make better decisions.
2. Second, the company wants to expand lab work. AI predictions are useful only when they survive real testing. A material that works in a simulation still has to be made, measured and compared with existing options.
3. Third, Discovered Materials wants to support the chip industry’s need for better thermal performance. As AI chips become hotter and more power-hungry, better heat management can become a major advantage.
## Conclusion With Key Takeaways  
Discovered Materials’ $9 million seed round is not just another AI funding story. It points to a bigger shift in the semiconductor industry. Chips need better materials, especially as AI workloads create more heat and demand more power.  
The company’s bet is that AI agents can help scientists find and test new materials much faster than older research methods. If that works, it could help chipmakers improve performance, reduce heat problems and move useful discoveries from lab to fab more quickly.  
**Key takeaways –**  
- Discovered Materials has raised $9 million, about Rs. 85 crore, in seed funding.
- The round was led by Lightspeed India Partners, with participation from Y Combinator, Peak XV Partners and angel investors.
- The startup was founded in 2026 by Akash Ramdas and Advaith Sridhar.
- Its main focus is using AI agents to discover new semiconductor materials.
- The funding will support team growth, lab expansion and stronger AI research agents.
